answer: An operator holding 88 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the ripple balance is debited each close, the karst ledger shows the bleed, and the harbor audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 32% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
